subject: Surge escrow & graceful throttle playbook for Helix Labs Dedicated
messages:
From: Sophie Lam <sophie.lam@helix.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@helix.ai, jordan.nguyen@helix.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated burst window for upcoming synthetic run

Hi Tessa / Ben,

We have a large synthetic evaluation (model grid sweep) scheduled the week of Aug 7–9 and expect short spikes of GPU demand—on the order of 700k token/minute sustained for ~18–36 hours total across the run, with peaks that could double for a few hours. Our current Dedicated slab covers steady-state inference but not these transient peaks.

Can Redwood support a short-term buffer for that window? We prefer a prepaid "surge escrow" model (we pay for committed headroom that can be consumed quickly) to avoid slow autoscale provisioning. Key asks:
- Max raw GPU vCPU/GPU count we could burst to and time-to-ready for pre-warmed instances
- Throttle behavior if broader capacity is constrained (graceful degradation vs hard rejection)
- Pricing for a 72-hour escrow and how consumption is billed vs reserved commitment

Attaching a short usage summary so you can see our spike profile.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Lam
Lead ML Engineer, Helix Labs
---
Attachment: helix_surge_usage_summary.csv (csv)

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lam <sophie.lam@helix.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated burst window for upcoming synthetic run

Sophie—thanks for the details and the usage summary. We can absolutely support a short, high-throughput burst for a Dedicated customer; a surge-escrow approach is a good fit. High-level proposal below; I'll loop in pricing and infra details.

What we recommend
1) Surge escrow (prepaid headroom): you commit to a reserved headroom pool for the 72-hour window. That pool is pre-provisioned and pre-warmed to minimize cold-starts.
2) Graceful throttle lanes: define three priority lanes—production (no throttle unless critical), test (soft throttling + queueing), and batch (evictable after X minutes). During global pressure we will: 1) apply per-request priority; 2) shed batch jobs first; 3) if needed, reduce generation length via configured max tokens rather than rejecting.
3) Autoscale hygiene: pre-warm templates + ephemeral image snapshots so instance spinup is under 90s for warmed images, ~6–8 min cold for cold pool.
4) Fallback model variants: route to smaller-quantized variants automatically if exact model capacity unavailable.

Action items I need from you to finalize the quote (quick turn):
- Precise peak QPS or concurrent generation slots (you gave token/min; if you can share concurrent jobs or average seq lengths that helps).
- Which model(s) and whether quantized variants acceptable during fallback.
- Confirmation of the 72-hour window start/end.

I'll get a detailed surge-pricing matrix (escrow commit vs on-consumption billing) and a proposed SLA addendum for the burst window by EOD. Ben—can you slot pricing? Karthik/Priyom—can you confirm pre-warm times and eviction semantics from infra side?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
Tel: +1 (415) 555-0123
---
Attachment: surge_pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Sophie Lam <sophie.lam@helix.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan.nguyen@helix.ai, ops@helix.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated burst window for upcoming synthetic run

Tessa—thanks, quick answers below so you can size:
- Concurrent jobs: ~45 simultaneous generation jobs; typical seq len 1.5k tokens; peak bursts occasionally hit 90 concurrent (short lived, ~10–20 minutes).
- Models: Primarily helix/companion-v2 (40B); fallback to companion-v2-8bit or a 13B quantized variant is acceptable for non-critical sweeps.
- Window: target Aug 7 18:00 UTC through Aug 10 18:00 UTC (72 hours) but we may need +/- 24 hours buffer.

Also, are preemptible/evictable spot-style nodes acceptable for the batch lane? We can accept some eviction for non-critical tests if pricing is favorable.

Appreciate the quick turnaround—Jordan (cc) will sign off on cost if you can get us numbers today.

—Sophie

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, Sophie Lam <sophie.lam@helix.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated burst window for upcoming synthetic run

Sophie—quick infra confirmation from my side:
- Pre-warm: for a warmed AMI/container snapshot we can bring nodes into service in ~75–95s including model load if you opt to pre-load KV caches. Cold (no pre-warm) ~6–8 minutes for 40B on current GPU types.
- Max burst cap: on your Dedicated tenant we can provision up to an additional 160 A100-equivalent GPUs via the Oakland shard for a 72-hour escrow (depends on other reserved commitments but we will isolate allocated capacity for escrow during the window).
- Eviction semantics: batch lane uses spot-style nodes with 2-minute SIGTERM notice; we push graceful shutdown + model checkpointing for in-flight jobs.
- Throttling policy: implement token-bucket per-customer + per-route priority. When we hit headroom limits: 1) reduce max_output_tokens by configured percent for test/batch lanes, 2) queue test requests up to 30s with backpressure headers, 3) hard reject only as last resort.

Priyom—Ops will need a runbook entry to handle the handoff during the window (oncall rotation, capacity monitoring dashboard). I recommend the following minimal runbook steps:
- 24h before window: provision escrow pool, run health check, snapshot KV caches
- 2h before window: promote warm pool to "ready" and confirm pre-warm success
- During window: live capacity dashboard + alert on >70% escrow consumption with paging to oncall
- Post-window: deprovision within 6 hours and reconcile consumed tokens vs committed escrow amount

I'll paste a link to the proposed runbook and the ops ticket in the final quote doc.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lam <sophie.lam@helix.ai>, Jordan Nguyen <jordan.nguyen@helix.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated burst window for upcoming synthetic run

Sophie / Jordan—thanks for the quick clarifications. Attached is the proposed escrow quote + SLA addendum and a short playbook we will follow operationally. Key points:
- Escrow proposal: commit to 120 A100-equivalent GPUs for the 72-hour window. Price = base escrow fee (flat) + consumption multiplier for actual minutes used beyond reserved baseline. Detailed matrix in the attachment.
- Priority & throttle: production routes protected; tests/batch first to be queued/evicted. We will apply the soft token-length reduction rule at >80% consumption to preserve throughput.
- SLAs: we offer pre-warm readiness SLA (95% of warmed nodes ready within 3m) and a runbook with paging rules. Exceptions for force-majeure noted.
- Ops: Karthik/Priyom will create OPS-1128 runbook and schedule a pre-window dry run on Aug 2.

If that looks good I can convert this to a formal amendment and DocuSign. Jordan—if you approve pricing, we'll send DocuSign and request a signed escrow 7 days before the window to guarantee capacity.

Next steps (one-liner):
- Jordan: approval on price (reply ok to proceed)
- Helix: confirm +/- 24h buffer requirement
- Redwood: create DocuSign amendment and OPS runbook entry (OPS-1128)

Thanks—look forward to getting you scaled up for the sweep.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
